summary: A satirical, humorous account of LaughingDollar Inc.'s absurdly complex expense reporting process, framed as a heroic quest. It walks through the stages of a 15-step method launched September 7th 2023: collecting original receipts, categorizing expenses, entering them in online forms, gaining manager approval, waiting for reimbursement, and surviving audits by Margaret Meticulous.
one_line: A satirical tale of LaughingDollar Inc.'s overly convoluted expense reporting, from original receipts to approvals, slow reimbursement and audits.
key_facts: LaughingDollar Inc. launched a new expense reporting method on September 7th 2023, described as a 'simplified' 15-step technique.
CFO Steve Ledger masterminded the 15-step expense reporting technique, designed to foster financial responsibility and accountability.
Employees must submit original receipts; any digital submission triggers an automated reply: 'Originals only, please.'
Sales representative Monica Quill once spent three hours deciding whether a $5 coffee was a miscellaneous beverage expense or incremental energy expenditure.
An internal memo from Steve Ledger dated September 25th 2023 said the online forms were optimized for 'maximum time consumption in order to enable deep contemplation of fiscal impact'.
Expenses must be entered line-by-line into the 'Oracle of Online Forms', a grid of dropdowns, text boxes and radio buttons.
Project manager John Dough says every request must pass through 'Nine Layers of Justification' before he signs digitally, and calls budget spreadsheets 'the one spreadsheet to rule them all'.
The extra breadstick at Olive Garden is a legendary expense justification tale at LaughingDollar.
Reimbursement supposedly follows lunar phases and pays out only during lunar eclipses; some employees call it the '90-day ordeal'.
Margaret 'The Magnifying Glass' Meticulous, the Overlord of Audits, can reportedly spot doctored taxi receipts from 50 paces away.
The piece is humorous exaggeration using fantasy and pop-culture references such as Merlin, Middle Earth, Sherlock Holmes and the Dewey Decimal system.
